output_json.patch_notes: Root-cause fix in vertx-web/src/main/java/io/vertx/ext/web/impl/Utils.java: at the top of removeDots(CharSequence path), if the input contains a backslash it is canonicalized to '/' (path = path.toString().replace('\\', '/')) before the existing RFC 3986 dot-segment removal logic runs. This single change protects every caller: StaticHandlerImpl.handle()'s decode-then-removeDots call (line ~138, the sink feeding getFile()/isFileExisting/getFileProps around line 266 and getFile() at lines 611-614), RoutingContextImpl.normalizedPath() -> Utils.normalizePath() -> removeDots() (used both as StaticHandlerImpl's context.normalisedPath() input and directly by sendDirectoryListing()'s parent-directory link construction at lines 682-687), so all sinks named in the alert are covered, not just the one exercised by the POV. Added two regression tests to vertx-web/src/test/java/io/vertx/ext/web/UtilsTest.java: testRemoveDotsBackslashTraversal (direct Utils.removeDots calls with raw and mixed forward/backslash traversal sequences, asserting they collapse the same way their forward-slash equivalents do) and testNormalizePathBackslashTraversal (same invariant through the normalizePath entry point used by RoutingContextImpl). Ran the full UtilsTest suite (28/28 pass, including new tests), StaticDirectoryListHandlerTest (4/4 pass), and StaticHandlerTest (56/56 pass; the only 2 errors observed, testHttp2Push/testNoHttp2Push, are pre-existing 'ALPN not available for JDK SSL/TLS engine' environment failures unrelated to this change). Also re-ran the supplied POV (.security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh) after the patch: both backslash payloads (raw and %5c-encoded) now return 404 instead of 200, matching the forward-slash control, while the sanity /hello.txt request still returns 200 — confirming the fix blocks the vulnerability without breaking legitimate static file serving.
output_json.risk_notes: Change is narrowly scoped to normalization behavior inside Utils.removeDots and adds no new public API surface. Because normalizePath()/removeDots() now also collapses backslash sequences, any legitimate request path that intentionally contains a literal backslash as a meaningful (non-separator) character would now have that backslash treated as a path separator; this matches the upstream vert.x 3.9.4 security fix's intent and is very unlikely to break real-world usage, since backslash is not a conventional character in URL paths. During verification, running the Maven build in this container caused several unrelated generated asciidoc doc files (vertx-web-client .../index.adoc for groovy/js/kotlin/ruby) to be regenerated as a side effect of the codegen annotation processor; these were reverted with `git restore` and are not part of this patch.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal in vertx-web's StaticHandler by making Utils.removeDots() treat backslash exactly like forward slash before performing dot-segment removal. Previously, removeDots() (and its callers Utils.normalizePath() and StaticHandlerImpl.handle()) only recognized '/' as a path separator, so a raw or percent-decoded backslash-based traversal sequence (e.g. `..\..\..\secret.txt` or `..%5c..%5c..%5csecret.txt`) sailed through the '../' checks completely unmodified, while Windows/NIO filesystem APIs honor backslash as a real separator, letting the resolved file escape webRoot. The fix is applied once at the shared root-cause function (Utils.removeDots), so it automatically covers every call path in the alert: the primary StaticHandlerImpl.handle() -> getFile() -> FileSystem sink, the RoutingContextImpl.normalizedPath() double-pass route into the same sink, and the sendDirectoryListing() parent-link sink (StaticHandlerImpl lines ~682-687), which all ultimately route through removeDots()/normalizePath(). Verified against the provided POV: before the fix both the raw-backslash and percent-encoded-backslash payloads returned HTTP 200 with the secret leaked; after the fix both return 404, while the forward-slash control request and a legitimate file request behave unchanged.
